silhouette.reason: panel-1: Front silhouette reads as an armoured orc bust: pointed ears, topknot, spiked pauldrons and tusks register in black. Side and rear read as a gourd/egg on a plinth; the cranium dome dominates, there is no jaw, brow or neck break, and the face is a shallow bump on the front of the egg. | panel-2: Front reads as an orc bust: pointed ears, topknot, two spiked pauldrons, tusks and beard. Side and rear read as a smooth egg or pear: one continuous ovoid from crown to chest with no neck, nape, trapezius or occipital break, so the shadow says 'gourd with shoulder pads' rather than 'orc'. Tusks are too small to break the profile, and the ears are thin slivers that disappear side-on. | panel-3: Front silhouette reads as a fantasy orc bust: pointed ears, topknot, spiked pauldrons and the plinth all break the outline. The side view is the weak one: the head is a smooth egg/gourd with a bulging occiput, the jaw and chin barely project, so in black the profile reads as a pear with a shoulder pad rather than a heavy-jawed orc. Tusks are too small to register in the silhouette at all.
fixes: Push the brow ridge and underbite jaw forward in side view so the profile shows a heavy brow shelf, flat nose bridge and protruding lower jaw
Carve a trapezius/neck transition so the head stops merging into the torso blob at the back
Enlarge the ears and tusks by ~30% so they break the outline in every view
Carve a neck and trapezius slope: pull the jaw/occiput mass in above the shoulder line so the side profile has a clear notch under the skull
Push the brow ridge and lower jaw forward 2-3 cm in profile; enlarge the lower tusks so they clear the upper lip and read in black
Thicken and angle the ears outward so they break the front and side outline
Push the lower jaw forward and widen it so the underbite and chin mass break the side profile
Lengthen and thicken the lower tusks (roughly 2x) so they poke past the upper lip line in front and side silhouettes
Flatten the back of the skull and add a thick trapezius/neck mass so the side view is not an egg on a ball

proportions.reason: panel-1: The cranium is far too tall and rounded for an orc: the face occupies only the lower third, eyes sit low and close under a huge dome, the forehead is a long smooth slope. Side view shows a pear-shaped skull with almost no depth from brow to occiput structure and a weak chin hidden by the beard. Pauldrons are oversized helmets relative to the shoulders and the torso has no readable pectoral/deltoid anatomy. | panel-2: The cranium is far too tall and deep for the face: the face sits on the lower third of a domed egg, the back of the skull runs straight into the shoulders, and there is no neck at all. Eyes are small and sit shallow with almost no orbit or brow shelf over them. The jaw is narrow for an orc (should be the widest part of the head with heavy masseters). Ears are thin and set low. Pauldrons are well scaled to the shoulders, but the torso under the beard reads as a soft blob with no pectoral or deltoid structure. | panel-3: Cranium is far too tall and domed relative to a small, recessed face; the face occupies only the lower front third of the head. Brow ridge is weak for an orc, nose is small and mushy, the mouth sits too low and narrow and the jaw is undersized. Eyes sit reasonably in the orbits, but the head reads more like a bald ogre/troll caricature than the heavy-browed, wide-jawed orc archetype. Ears are set high and slightly back, acceptable. Torso is a soft blob without clavicle or pectoral structure.
fixes: Lower the skull vault by ~20% and widen the zygomatic/jaw region so the face fills half the head height
Raise the eye line to roughly mid-head and set eyes deeper into defined orbits under a brow ridge
Build a wide, square mandible with the lower canines rooted in it; add a short thick neck with sternocleidomastoid and trapezius masses
Scale pauldrons down ~15% and seat them on sculpted deltoids
Lower the vertex of the skull ~15% and shorten the back of the cranium; widen the jaw and cheekbones so face width is greater than cranium width
Add a heavy supraorbital ridge and sink the eyes into orbits under it
Build a short thick neck and sterno/trapezius masses between head and chest; add pectoral and deltoid planes under the pauldrons
Thicken the ears at the root and raise them to eye-to-brow level
Reduce cranial height ~15% and bring the hairline/brow forward so the face takes up more of the head
Sculpt a pronounced supraorbital ridge and a broad flat nose with flared nostrils
Widen the mandible and mouth to near cheekbone width; raise the mouth slightly
Add clavicle, sternocleidomastoid and pectoral planes to the chest so the bust has anatomy below the beard

materials.reason: panel-1: Skin, leather belt, bone tusks/spikes and dark iron separate by hue and value, but the iron is a flat matte grey with almost no specular response, the skin has no subsurface or roughness breakup, and the back fur mantle reads as brown clay rather than hide or fur. The glowing eyes are the one strong material note. | panel-2: Skin, iron, leather, bone and hair separate by hue, and the skin has a mottled albedo. But the iron pauldrons are a flat uniform dark grey plastic with a soft generic highlight, no metallic response or roughness variation; the rust is circular stamped blotches. Bone spikes and tusks share one creamy plastic look. The skin has no subsurface warmth, the pale streaks on the face read like texture smears, and the beard is a dark smudge of strands. | panel-3: Skin, metal, leather, fur and bone separate by hue, and the glowing eyes read. But the steel pauldrons are uniform mid-grey with soft broad highlights, closer to plastic than worked iron; the leather strap and fur pelt are smooth, waxy surfaces with no grain or fibre; the topknot hair looks like melted clay. Skin has some mottling but no subsurface or roughness variation around nose, lips and brow.
fixes: Give pauldron iron metalness ~0.9 with roughness variation (polished edges, rougher hollows) so it reflects the environment
Add sheen/subsurface tint and oily roughness breakup on the skin (nose, forehead, lips)
Replace the clay mantle with a fur/hide strip: card fur or strand alpha along the edge, sheen finish
Give the pauldrons true metallic PBR with roughness breakup: polished edges, darker rough cavities, rust that runs from rivets downward instead of round dots
Separate bone (spikes, tusks, teeth) with yellowed cavity tint and lower roughness at tips
Add warm red tint in ears, nose, lips and eyelids to sell skin; remove or rework the pale vertical streaks on the face into proper scar tissue
Give the beard clumped cards with a lighter tip gradient instead of a dark smear
Give the pauldrons a darker, rougher base with sharp edge highlights and a hammered-metal roughness map
Add fibre/strand normal detail to the fur mantle and topknot instead of smooth tubes
Add leather grain and edge darkening to the belt/strap; vary skin roughness (oilier nose/forehead)

detail.reason: panel-1: Beard strands, rivets, a buckle, a bead necklace and a forehead scar exist, but the skin is almost featureless at close range: no pores, wrinkles, nasolabial folds, knuckle-like brow creases or veins. The detail-density heat map shows large flat zones on the skull and pauldrons. | panel-2: LOD0 has rivets, riveted rims on the pauldrons, a belt with buckle, a bead necklace, a fur mantle and a topknot with wrap. But the face is under-sculpted for a hero bust: no wrinkles, pores, nasolabial folds, lip definition or brow creases; the nose is a soft lump. Raking light shows the skull as almost perfectly smooth. Rivets are evenly spaced dots with no head shape. The topknot strands are tube-like and the fur mantle is a smooth sheet with a ragged edge. | panel-3: Rivets, buckle, bead necklace and banded vambraces exist, and the beard has strand cards. fixes: Add a skin height graph: pores, forehead wrinkles, crow's feet, nasolabial and brow furrows, veins at the temple
Model the nose with flared nostrils and a broken bridge; give lips thickness and a corner fold
Add plate overlaps, straps and buckles under the pauldrons and denser, varied rivets
Enlarge and irregularise the lower teeth; add chips to the tusks
Sculpt secondary/tertiary face forms: brow furrows, nasolabial folds, defined lips over the tusks, cheek and forehead scars with raised edges
Add skin pore/normal detail on head and shoulders so raking light shows texture
Model rivet heads as domes with a rim and add plate seams/hammer dents on the pauldrons
Break the fur mantle into tufted clumps and the hair into thinner braids with wraps
Sculpt forehead furrows, nasolabial folds, crow's feet and a real recessed scar with raised edges
Model ear helix/antihelix folds and a few notches or piercings
Separate the dreadlocks into individual tapered strands with wraps/beads
Model individual teeth with gum line and chips; add edge bevels and dents on pauldron rims

Nothing tells where this orc has been. | panel-3: Some rust-red spotting on the pauldrons, a painted scar and a ragged-edged pelt hint at history, but the armour has no dents, scratches or edge wear, the skin has no grime in creases, the leather is clean and the whole asset is fairly symmetrical. It looks freshly made rather than lived in by a warrior.

Add edge chips and dents on pauldron rims and a broken spike tip on one side
Add asymmetry: a notched ear, a chipped tusk, extra scars or war paint across the face
Add edge wear and dents to the pauldrons, asymmetric damage (one broken or chipped spike)
Run rust streaks downward from rivets and pool grime in the plate overlaps
Crack and darken the belt leather at folds and buckle; stain the necklace beads
Make the face asymmetric: one chipped tusk, a notched ear, a deeper scar across one eye
Add dents, gouges and bright scratched edges on pauldrons; rust streaks running down from rivets
